reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). I read the snapshot to check the plan against the code. The plan is mostly sound and grounded in it. pr_commits, PrCommit, closing_jobs with its CLOSING list, not_landed, fingerprint(git, treeish, rules_commit), diff_tree, verification_id and LandingCommit::validate all exist where the plan says. Its analysis that operator/ is governed in this repo is correct. It removes the trailers rather than adding exceptions, and its demonstrations would fail without the new behaviour. One major gap: Decision 3 requires candidate, verification and outcome to be added in the same commit. That refuses the real blocked-then-retried landing, which adds only outcome-landed.json (run.rs retry_landing), even though the gate accepts it. That contradicts the goal that real PRs stop being refused. Relaxing the rule to 'adds a landed outcome; the candidate and verification are present in the tree', with a test for that shape, would make the plan acceptable. Findings: major: Requiring candidate, verification and outcome to be added in the same commit refuses a blocked job that is later landed. (Decision 3; Demonstration for criterion 2(b)); minor: The realistic-range test passes only because the fixture adds an operator/ exclusion that this repository does not have. (Decision 4; Demonstration for criterion 1); nit: Running `cargo test -p athena-gate invariant` goes beyond the brief's 'run only the athena-core land and gh tests'. (Step 7)
